Combine the mating-unit forest into visNetwork-ready diagram data

Source: R/makePedigreeDiagramData.R
makePedigreeMatingLayout.Rd

Builds a kinship2-style pedigree layout in which each mating (a sire and dam pair) is drawn as a union node between the parents and their offspring. Returns the same list(nodes, edges) shape that makePedigreeDiagramData returns, plus a lookup table that maps each duplicate node id to the real individual it stands for. makePedigreeDiagramData itself is unaffected; this is a separate function.

Usage

makePedigreeMatingLayout(
  ped,
  edgeStyle = c("rectilinear", "direct"),
  twinRelations = NULL,
  kinshipMatrix = NULL,
  hints = NULL,
  maxNameChars = 15,
  conditionColors = c("#CC79A7", "#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73"),
  conditionThresholds = NULL
)

Arguments

ped

data frame with id, sire, dam, sex, and gen columns, same contract as makePedigreeDiagramData. An optional status column marks deceased animals: see the deceased column of the returned nodes. Every column whose name starts affected is an affected condition, in the order the data frame holds them, the first four drawn (see conditions in the return value). A lone one fills the symbol, in the first of conditionColors (pink by default) where the animal is affected and grey where its status is unknown (NA); two or more split it into sections, one colour each. (makePedigreeDiagramData reads the column affected alone.) A condition drawn reads as makePedigreeDiagramData()'s affected does: a number other than 0 and 1 stops, before any animal is left out. An optional genotyped column marks the genotyped animals (what kinship2 and Pedixplorer call available): TRUE, FALSE or NA (not recorded) for each animal, or 1 and 0, or text as.logical() reads ("TRUE", "false", "T"). A genotyped animal's symbol is drawn with its outline 4 pixels wide, every other symbol's 1 (see borderWidth in the returned nodes), and its hover text says “Genotyped: Yes”, “No” or “Unknown”; any other value stops, naming the column, before any animal is left out.

edgeStyle

one of "rectilinear" (default), which routes mate-line and sibship-bar edges through invisible waypoint nodes so they render as a strict right angle, kinship2-style, or "direct", which draws a straight edge from each parent to their mating unit and from each mating unit to each child.

twinRelations

optional data.frame with columns id1, id2, code (see checkTwinRelations). Not validated here; validate with checkTwinRelations first. NULL (default) adds no connector edges. A connector always targets the two individuals' real node ids and always renders as a direct edge regardless of edgeStyle.

kinshipMatrix

optional precomputed kinship matrix (a base matrix or a Matrix) with row AND column names set to individual ids. When supplied, it replaces this function's internal kinship() call as the sole source of the consanguineous-mating-unit flags (kinshipMatrix[sire, dam] > 0): twinRelations then drives twin connector edges only, so a caller wanting twin-corrected consanguinity must bake it into the matrix (e.g. kinship(..., twinRelations = ...)). A sire/dam id absent from the matrix's dimnames leaves that unit at the safe FALSE default, exactly as a dangling parent does on the default path. NULL (default) computes kinship(ped$id, ped$sire, ped$dam, ped$gen, twinRelations = twinRelations).

hints

NULL (default: the layout's own order) or a list with the elements order and mate, either one or both. order is a numeric vector named by ids in ped, as kinship2's and Pedixplorer's layout hints give it. Only the order of the numbers matters. Siblings, separate families and founder couples are drawn left to right in increasing order of their numbers; equal numbers keep the order of the rows of ped, and an animal the order does not name keeps its row's place. A founder couple is placed by its female's number (a male whose mate is not named, by his own), as kinship2 and Pedixplorer place them. In a family whose founders the order names, the layout's own reordering of founder lines (which shortens the lines joining an animal drawn twice) is not done. An order may put a sibling between twins; the twin line then crosses it. mate is a data frame with one row per mating to place and the columns left, right and anchor: left and right are a sire and a dam with offspring together in ped, in either column, and left is drawn left of right at their mating; anchor ("left", "right" or "either") names the partner whose own place the offspring are drawn under, the other partner then drawn beside it as a repeat node when it has parents of its own, and "either" keeps the layout's own choice. As kinship2 draws its spouse hint, the offspring of an animal's several matings follow its mates' sides, mates hinted to one side are drawn left to right in the order of the rows, and mates not hinted are drawn nearest the animal. A hint can change where the layout draws matings it does not name. list(), and order or mate NULL or empty, give the layout of no hint. Stops on an element other than order and mate; on an order that is not numeric, a number without a name, a name given twice or not in ped, and NA; and on a mate that is not a data frame or lacks a column, NA, the same id as left and right, an id not in ped (a sire or dam without a row of its own), a pair with no offspring together or named twice, an anchor other than those three, and an anchor on the partner of an earlier generation than its mate (the layout draws a mating on the row of its later partner). The returned hints are the hints the layout used, in this form: passed back, they give the same layout, so an edit can start from the layout's own order (see the example).

maxNameChars

the most characters of an animal's name written in label under its id, on its node and on each of its repeat nodes, 15 by default: a longer name is cut there and ends in "...", while title keeps it whole. A line break counts as one character. Inf writes every name whole, as kinship2 and Pedixplorer write their labels; a long name can then run into the labels of the animals beside it. It changes nothing but the labels. Stops unless it is one whole number of 1 or more, or Inf.

conditionColors

the colours of the affected conditions, in the order they are drawn: 1 to 4 colours, at least one for each condition drawn, each a name R knows (such as "orange" or "steelblue3") or a code (such as "#E69F00"). Each is written as its "#RRGGBB" code, the colour R means by it: a browser reads most of R's names as no colour, and "grey", "gray", "green", "maroon" and "purple" as other colours. The default is the four colours drawn before this argument: pink, orange, sky blue and bluish green, the last three Okabe and Ito's colour-blind-safe ones. They fill the symbols here and go into the returned conditions table, from which drawPedigreeDiagram paints the sections and the legend, so all three agree. With no condition column nothing is coloured, and the drawing's one “Affected” legend row keeps the default pink. Stops on anything but 1 to 4 colours as text, on NA, on a colour R does not know, on a number (it picks from R's palette, which can be changed), on a transparent colour, on white and on the grey "#BEBEBE" (they mark an unaffected animal and an unknown status), on a colour given twice, and on fewer colours than conditions drawn.

conditionThresholds

NULL (the default), or the cut-offs of measured traits: a character vector named by condition columns, each a comparison, >, >=, < or <=, and a number, such as c(affected_glucose = ">= 126", affected_hb = "< 13"). An animal whose number passes its column's cut-off is drawn affected, one whose number does not is drawn unaffected, and one with no number (NA) is drawn as unknown. The rule goes into the condition's label, so the legend and the tooltip state it, >= and <= written as the signs for at least and at most: “Affected (glucose >= 126)” with the sign; the tooltip also gives the animal's number, “Yes (140)”. A column without a cut-off is read as before, and a number in it other than 0 and 1 stops. Stops on anything but a named character vector, on a cut-off it cannot read, on a name that is not a condition column of ped, and on a column with a cut-off that does not hold numbers.

Value

A list with nodes (id, label, shape, title, size, color.background, deceased (logical, never NA: TRUE for the node of an animal whose status reads DECEASED, and for each of its repeat-appearance nodes, FALSE for every other node and for all of them when ped has no status column), x, y; color.border is added under edgeStyle = "rectilinear"; affectedSections is added when there are two or more conditions: a character string with one character per condition, "1" where the animal is affected, "0" where it is unaffected and "?" where it is unknown (the drawing fills that section grey), the same for a repeat-appearance node as for its animal, "" for a node that is not an animal, never NA; with two or more conditions the animals' color.background is white, the sections carrying the color; borderWidth is added when ped has a genotyped column: 4 for the node of a genotyped animal and each of its repeat-appearance nodes, 1 for every other node, the width of the symbol's outline), edges (from, to, dashes, smooth.enabled, smooth.type, smooth.roundness, color, width; the color and width columns are always present once any mating unit exists: a consanguineous mating unit's (kinship(sire, dam) > 0) 2 spouse-to-union edges get "#D55E00"/4, an Okabe-Ito colorblind-safe vermillion in kinship2's doubled/thickened mate-line convention, and every other edge gets NA; label is added when twinRelations is supplied), and duplicateToReal (a named character vector, duplicate node id -> real individual id). Under edgeStyle = "rectilinear", an already-set edge color (e.g. the twin connector's or the consanguinity marker's) is preserved when the edge is kept as-is; a marked mate edge that gets replaced by a right-angle projection currently falls back to the generic routing color and width. Also isolatedIds, a character vector of ids suppressed from nodes/edges because they have no known parent, are never a parent, and are not connected by twinRelations; it is character(0) when nothing was suppressed. When every individual in ped is isolated, nodes/edges are both 0-row and duplicateToReal is empty. Also conditions, a data frame with one row per drawn condition (column, label such as “Affected” or “Affected (diabetes)”, and its color, from conditionColors as a "#RRGGBB" code), 0-row when ped has no such column, and conditionsNotDrawn, the names of any such columns past the fourth. Last, hints, the hints the layout used, in the form the argument hints takes, so that passing them back gives the same layout: order numbers each animal drawn that has a parent by its row in the rows the layout drew from (an order hint applied, the animals left out not counted), and a founder only where an order hint named it, since naming a founder turns off the layout's own ordering of founder lines; mate holds the rows of a mate hint as given, then a row for each other mating whose sire and dam both have rows in ped, left and right as drawn and anchor the partner the offspring hang under, except the matings of an animal that anchors three or more matings or that the given rows place, where a row can change how far its mates are drawn. With every animal left out, order has no numbers and mate no rows.

Details

Mating-unit nodes render as a small, unlabeled dot with an offspring-count tooltip, visually distinct from the 5 sex-coded shapes. An individual who has to appear more than once in the layout gets duplicate nodes. A duplicate node keeps the real individual's own shape, label and tooltip content (plus a cue that it is a duplicate), so it reads as that individual, and is connected to it by a dashed edge.

In the default "rectilinear" edge style, mate-line and sibship-bar edges are routed through invisible waypoint nodes so they render as strict right angles, as kinship2 draws them. In the "direct" edge style, edges are straight segments from each parent to the mating unit and from the mating unit to each child.

A simple two-real-parent mating unit (each parent has exactly one mate and both have unambiguous "M"/"F" sex codes) is drawn with the male parent to the left of the female parent. The final horizontal positions come from a joint quadratic program that preserves each row's provisional left-to-right order, so this rule carries into the rendered layout. It cannot be turned off, unless a mate hint says otherwise (see hints).

Examples

## Seven animals: C and D are full siblings, and so are F and G, D's
## offspring
ped <- data.frame(
  id = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, "A", "A", NA, "D", "D"),
  dam = c(NA, NA, "B", "B", NA, "E", "E"),
  sex = c("M", "F", "F", "M", "F", "M", "F"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
ped$gen <- findGeneration(ped$id, ped$sire, ped$dam)
layout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(ped)

## The hints the layout used: passed back, the same layout
layout$hints
#> $order
#> C D F G 
#> 3 4 6 7 
#> 
#> $mate
#>   left right anchor
#> 1    A     B   left
#> 2    D     E   left
#> 
identical(makePedigreeMatingLayout(ped, hints = layout$hints), layout)
#> [1] TRUE

## Edited: G drawn left of F
hints <- layout$hints
hints$order[c("F", "G")] <- hints$order[c("G", "F")]
swapped <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(ped, hints = hints)
